_note: Divergences between source-prep.js and the expectations committed before the first run (fd6a58a). Recorded as observed on 2026-10-06 against source-prep/0.1.0. Not fixed: a fix tuned on these same cases would only show that it fits them, so any fix must also be checked on new constructed cases written before the fix is run. The runner fails if a divergence appears, disappears or changes, so this record is kept equal to the code. UPDATE 2026-10-06: all six were resolved in source-prep/0.3.0. Each entry keeps its original observation and gains resolved_in and resolution; the runner now requires these cases to match.
observations: R02 matches, but its exception basis is recognised only because the word 'given' appears in 'Approval was given', not from its basis clause 'on the basis that'. A correct result for the wrong reason.

2026-10-06: re-run against source-prep/0.2.0 (instruction-like text detection added). The same 18 cases match and the same six divergences recur, unchanged; no regression case contains instruction-like text.

R18.explanation: The word list treats any 'clearly' as an assertion without basis. A finding a reviewer can dismiss; nothing is refused.
R18.status: RESOLVED (history preserved; the original observation above is unchanged)

resolution.general_rule: 'clearly' followed by a presentation or perception word ('printed') is descriptive
resolution.evidence: Re-run of this 24-case set against source-prep/0.3.0: the case now matches its expectation, which was not edited (fd6a58a). Confirmation corpus v0.1.0 (759ea86, committed before the fix): 47 of 47 after the fix, 24 of 47 before it.
resolution.limit: The same author wrote the confirmation cases and the rule, with the intended rule in mind. The result shows the rule behaves as designed on constructed cases; it is not independent evidence that it generalises.
